summary: The petitioners, medical students aspiring to appear for NEET-PG 2022, challenged the deadline for completion of internship, initially set at 31 May 2022 and later extended to 31 July 2022. They argued that due to delayed commencement of internships caused by deployment in Covid-19 duties in several states, they would be unable to meet the deadline. They sought either a further extension or recognition of Covid duties as part of internship. The Court acknowledged hardship but emphasized judicial restraint in academic policy matters. Relying on precedents, it held that setting eligibility criteria is within executive and regulatory domain, and courts should not interfere unless arbitrary or discriminatory. Practical challenges in disrupting the exam schedule and integrity of curriculum were considered.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur & Ors. v. Soutrik Sarangi
All India Council for Technical Education v. Surinder Kumar Dhawan
Rachna v. Union of India & Ors.
final_judgment: The petition was dismissed, upholding the internship completion deadline of 31 July 2022, deferring to executive authority in academic and policy matters.
